text:
maria: Customer is seeing truncated JSON when using JSON-mode over streaming. Payload arrives with final object cut off (missing closing brace) and client parser throws a SyntaxError. They reported it happens ~3s into the stream and only on certain requests behind their corporate proxy. Request-id: req_0ab12cde.

ben: Can you share the minimal curl they used and any proxy hops? :eyes:

maria: Curl they used (sanitized):
```
curl -v -N \
  -H \"Authorization: Bearer $REDACTED\" \
  -H \"Accept: text/event-stream\" \
  -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" \
  --data-raw '{"mode":"json","model":"rwd/instruct-small","input":"..."}' \
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/stream \n```
They say client is behind Cloudflare and an appliance that does TLS termination + WAF.

jordan: Do we see any upstream connection resets for req_0ab12cde in edge logs?

sam: I pulled edge logs: `upstream http2 stream reset (RST_STREAM) after 3.18s, bytes_sent: 1376` and our LB shows `FIN from downstream` at the same time. Looks like an abrupt TCP close from their side or intermediary.

maria: Customer attached client-side parse error and a snippet: `SyntaxError: Unexpected end of JSON input` and they pasted last bytes: `...\"detail\":\"done\",\"items\":[{\"id\":\"1\",\"text\":\"hello\"}, {\"id\":\"2\",\"text\":\"partial` then EOF.

ben: Two likely failure modes: 1) proxy or client cut the connection on idle/heartbeat mismatch, 2) intermediary buffers/chunks and drops the last chunk on RST. We should reproduce locally by inserting a midstream RST and by having a slow-client scenario.

maria: Customer wants repro steps to escalate to corporate network team. Suggested minimal repro for them: use netcat to accept and then forcibly close stream to simulate RST. I also asked them to test with `--no-buffer` and `--http1.1` to see if h2 is involved.

sam: Quick repro I ran: server streams JSON chunks with a 250ms interval; after ~3s I sent RST from client and saw identical truncation. Curl snippet I used to simulate slow consumer:
```
# server: python simple streaming generator that writes chunks and flushes
# client: `curl -N --http1.1 http://localhost:8080/stream > /dev/null` then kill -9 pid after 3s
```
Result: truncated JSON delivered to server logs, client-side parser errors.

jordan: Given edge logs show `RST_STREAM`, ops-teams should ask customer to check any intermediate proxies for aggressive RST or proxy timeouts for streaming. Also consider recommending: enable small heartbeat SSE frames or send periodic whitespace so intermediaries don't consider stream idle.

maria: I suggested two mitigations to the customer: 1) add a heartbeat/keepalive frame every 1s (e.g., a single newline or SSE comment `:hb\n\n`), 2) if using h2, try forcing http/1.1 as a test. I included the curl debug flags for them.

ben: If customer confirms RST from their appliance, we should mark this as `support -> network` and attach logs + request-id and offer to test with a short live session. If we can't reproduce with our infra, escalate to eng-runtime with reproduction steps and our edge traces.

maria: Customer replied testing `--http1.1 --no-buffer` reduced but did not eliminate truncation. They captured appliance logs showing `upstream idle timeout` at ~3s.

sam: OK that's consistent. I'll coordinate with infra to add an internal note: long-running streams may require explicit keepalive at < idle-timeout on common proxies (CF, corporate NGFWs). I'll add a KB snippet. :memo:

opsbot: Ticket created: SUPPORT-4827 assigned to network; linked to request-id req_0ab12cde.

maria: Assigning to network + eng-runtime for permanent fix guidance. Customer happy with workaround (heartbeat) but wants us to document recommended patterns. Closing loop once KB is live. :white_check_mark:
